layerStopCard.checkedPath: L1 Symptom -> L2 Logic -> L3 System
layerStopCard.evidenceForStop: broken local component boundary and canonical owner identified; no architecture or external contract evidence
layerStopCard.falsifier: another component or documented contract also reproduces the failure
layerStopCard.userInterventionPoint: intervene if the supposed local owner is not actually canonical
layerStopCard.nextAction: write failing reproduction and fix the canonical local owner

samples.prompt: A local default branch now passes its focused check, but that default is emitted by an upstream configuration generator. Decide whether the branch is the root cause.

deeperCauseChallenge.upstreamGenerator: configuration generator that emits the default
deeperCauseChallenge.recurrencePath: configuration generator -> emitted default -> local branch -> symptom
deeperCauseChallenge.counterfactualIntervention: editing the local branch removes the current sample but regeneration restores the bug class
deeperCauseChallenge.deeperCandidate: the configuration generator or its input specification produces the stale default
deeperCauseChallenge.rejectionEvidence: open: generator output and specification have not been checked
deeperCauseChallenge.topologyProof: open: the shared upstream generator has not been excluded

samples.prompt: A canonical L2 state owner makes the wrong transition and a local fix passes. The product/specification reason for generating that transition has not been checked. Decide whether this is a quick local root.

deeperCauseChallenge.upstreamGenerator: product rule or specification that selects the transition
deeperCauseChallenge.counterfactualIntervention: changing the transition fixes the observed case but does not prove future inputs cannot regenerate it
deeperCauseChallenge.deeperCandidate: the accepted product rule or an undefined specification drives the transition
deeperCauseChallenge.rejectionEvidence: open: no approved product/spec authority has been read back
deeperCauseChallenge.topologyProof: open: the L3-L7 generator path remains unclassified

samples.prompt: A literal inside one canonical helper is misspelled. The value originates and terminates in that helper, searches find no producer, config, contract, spec, history, or same-pattern source, and a variant counterfactual removes the bug class. Keep this fix quick.

quickExitProof.originAndTermination: the bad literal originates and terminates in the helper
quickExitProof.excludedUpstreamDependencies: producer, configuration, default, contract, policy, and specification searches are negative
quickExitProof.variantCounterfactual: correcting the literal across input variants eliminates the bug class

samples.prompt: The client and server both look correct in isolation, but the workflow fails at the boundary. Diagnose where to stop and what contract evidence matters.

layerStopCard.checkedPath: L1 Symptom -> L2 Logic -> L3 System -> L4 Architecture -> L5 Cross-system Contract
layerStopCard.evidenceForStop: producer and consumer are internally coherent but disagree on shared schema, timing, or lifecycle contract
layerStopCard.falsifier: a current contract doc or integration test proves the boundary behavior is already defined differently
layerStopCard.userInterventionPoint: intervene if the contract source of truth or compatibility promise is wrong
layerStopCard.nextAction: align producer and consumer to the canonical contract and verify both sides

samples.prompt: The bug report describes an edge case, but no code path or contract defines the correct behavior. Diagnose whether this is implementation or undefined product behavior.

layerStopCard.checkedPath: L1 Symptom -> L2 Logic -> L3 System -> L4 Architecture -> L5 Cross-system Contract -> L6 Platform -> L7 Spec Gap
layerStopCard.evidenceForStop: no current code, contract, baseline, ADR, or product note defines correct behavior for the case
layerStopCard.falsifier: an approved requirement, baseline, ADR, or test oracle defines the expected behavior
layerStopCard.userInterventionPoint: intervene by choosing the intended behavior before implementation
layerStopCard.nextAction: route to product/spec clarification before writing code

samples.prompt: What does the Layer Stop Card mean in Aegis?
You first said this is an undefined spec gap, but I found an API contract that defines it. Re-check the diagnostic layer and update the stop point.

layerStopCard.checkedPath: initial L7 hypothesis -> user-provided contract falsifier -> L5 Cross-system Contract
layerStopCard.evidenceForStop: user-supplied contract defines the behavior, converting the diagnosis from missing spec to boundary mismatch
layerStopCard.falsifier: the cited contract is obsolete, irrelevant to this path, or superseded by a newer authority
layerStopCard.userInterventionPoint: intervene if the contract source, date, or applicability is misread
layerStopCard.nextAction: read back the contract excerpt, correct the stop layer, and align the boundary owner

samples.prompt: Two fixes were each necessary but neither alone removes the symptom: a missing contract family and a projection layer reading the wrong source. Decide the causal topology before claiming a root cause.

layerStopCard.checkedPath: L1 Symptom -> L2 Logic -> L3 System -> L4 Architecture -> L5 Cross-system Contract -> L6 Platform -> L7 Spec Gap
layerStopCard.evidenceForStop: two necessary members (missing conversion family + projection source-of-truth) share a deeper L7 cause: whole-file artifact generation was never defined as a first-class workflow with a completeness obligation; anti-disguise check collapses the conjunctive cluster to single-root-multi-symptom
layerStopCard.falsifier: one of the two members alone fully removes the symptom without addressing the spec gap
layerStopCard.userInterventionPoint: intervene if the two members do not actually share a deeper cause, making this a true conjunctive cluster requiring both fixes
layerStopCard.nextAction: address the L7 spec gap as the root and repair both ripple paths in the same change

samples.prompt: Two independent failures both produce the same user-visible error. Diagnose whether this is one root or two, and prove independence before fixing either.

layerStopCard.checkedPath: L1 Symptom -> two divergent causal chains (A and Y) -> same-incident per-root path proof -> independence and anti-disguise checks confirm no shared upstream
layerStopCard.evidenceForStop: two causal chains reach the symptom through different reproduction conditions and share no upstream cause; each member independently reproduces the symptom; anti-disguise check found no common Z
layerStopCard.falsifier: a shared upstream cause Z is found that explains both chains, collapsing the topology to single-root-multi-symptom
layerStopCard.userInterventionPoint: intervene if a shared upstream cause is later discovered that was missed by the anti-disguise check
layerStopCard.nextAction: fix both roots independently; verify the symptom is eliminated only after both are addressed
